title: The editor cannot tell 'no rule set stored' from 'stored but ETag header hidden' when the stored set is empty (no rules, no own domains): it sends If-None-Match: * and the server answers 412
evidence: GET /calendar/join-rules returns the same body shape for an unstored and a stored-but-empty set; the contract's only signal is the ETag header. looksStored() treats rules.length>0 || ownDomains.length>0 as stored. A stored EMPTY set whose ETag is missing (older API, CORS not exposing it) is therefore treated as 'create', the PUT carries If-None-Match: *, and a correct API answers 412 'someone else changed it'. Safe (nothing overwritten) but the message is misleading and the Reload action then loops to the same state. A non-empty stored set with no ETag is correctly refused before any PUT.
fix_direction: Have the API mark the stored/unstored distinction in the GET body (e.g. a boolean) or always send ETag; the web then keys 'save unavailable' off that instead of the heuristic.

title: No test pins that caller-supplied apiFetch headers cannot override the Authorization header; moving the options.headers spread after authorization survives the whole join-rules + api suite
evidence: Mutation M5 (spread options.headers AFTER authorization): 140/140 tests still pass (src/pages/join-rules + src/api). The manifest claims the header cannot override authorization or content-type; true in the code, asserted nowhere. Latent today: the only caller passing headers sends If-Match / If-None-Match.
fix_direction: Add a client.test.ts case: apiFetch with headers {authorization:Bearer evil, content-type:text/plain} sends the real Bearer key and application/json. Verify inside the next unit touching client.ts; no separate unit.
